title: Continuous queue surge autopsy notes
content:
Summary:
This is a personal autopsy-style scratchpad for the Feb 26 throughput regression that looks like repeated short-duration queue surges. The pattern: sustained throughput drop (~20-35%) for 10-30 minutes at a time across multiple clusters, with tail latencies unchanged for single-request paths but average per-token cost spiking and allocator occupancy increasing. Suspect continuous-batcher misconfiguration + workload skew + misapplied prefill settings.

Micro-timeline (local notes):
- 2026-02-26 10:20 UTC: first pager; host groups in eu-west saw throughput decline.
- 2026-02-26 10:23 UTC: CSM reported application retries increased.
- 2026-02-26 10:28 UTC: mitigation: rolled traffic to smaller model variant in eu-west; local throughput recovered, global still degraded.
- 2026-02-26 10:45 UTC: engineers noticed queue depth oscillations and small sustained increases in prefill churn counter.
- 2026-02-26 11:05 UTC: root cause hypothesis #1 emerged: continuous-batcher window misalignment after rolling config change (prefill_threshold lowered).

What I observed in runtime telemetry (interesting counters):
- prefill_churn.rate: spiky, correlates with throughput drop windows
- active_prefills.count: +40% during incidents
- slot_occupancy_avg: up ~0.3 -> 0.6 (normalized)
- batch_build_attempts_per_sec: slight increase, but batches fewer tokens per batch
- kv_cache.hit_rate: small dip (~2%) during surge windows
- continuous_batch_window_ms: config shunted from 50ms -> 8ms on some nodes in env patch

Key hypotheses (ranked):
1) Rolling config flip: a staged deploy accidentally set continuous_batch.window_ms too low for a subset of nodes. That caused more frequent but smaller batches; combined with prefill policy this increased per-token cost and introduced slot occupancy thrash.
2) Client traffic change: a bursty client started sending many short-seq requests; continuous-batcher couldn't amortize overhead and prefill churn increased.
3) Prefill eviction bug: a timing edge case evicted KV-prefill entries prematurely, forcing repeated prefill work on repeated prefixes.
4) Autoscaler interaction: the autoscaler removed nodes during low-util windows, then addition of traffic created transient oversubscription and queueing.

Commands and experiments I ran (ordered, with results):
1) Quick repro on staging (short sequences):
   - Run: ./tools/loadgen --model gpt-sm --qps 150 --seq 64 --duration 600s
   - Observed: steady batches, window_ms=50 -> throughput stable.
2) Flip window_ config to 10ms on a single staging pod:
   - kubectl -n inference set env deploy/continuous-batcher CONT_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=10
   - Logs: saw batch size drop from avg 512 tokens -> ~80 tokens; prefill_churn++
   - Result: per-token latency increased by 18%; occupancy rose.
3) Reproduce prefill churn with synthetic repeated prefixes:
   - python scripts/prefill_spammer.py --prefix "Hello" --rate 200
   - Runtime log snippet: "prefill:evict candidate=0.39 threshold=0.4 evicted=1" repeated
   - Interpretation: entries on the boundary of eviction threshold get churned under burst
4) Inspect allocator and slab usage:
   - rwictl inspect heap --pod batcher-3 | grep slab
   - Found: medium slab fragmentation spike during incident windows (20% more free small slabs)
5) Telemetry correlation check (simple grep):
   - elasticsearch query: count where continuous_batch_window_ms=10 and prefill_churn.rate>5
   - Matched ~30 nodes across eu-west clusters matching incident timestamps

Error snippets and logs (excerpts):
- [batcher-3] WARN prefill_manager.go:142: "prefill eviction: candidate below tolerance, evicting to satisfy occupancy"
- [batcher-7] INFO batch_builder.go:278: "built batch tokens=68 requests=12 window_ms=8"
- [allocator] ERROR slab_allocator.go:93: "unable to serve allocation: no free small-slab, waiting"

Config diffs discovered (from deploy history):
- 2026-02-25 03:12 UTC: chef/configs/continuous-batcher.yml staged change: window_ms: 50 -> 10 (canary fraction 10%)
- 2026-02-25 03:16 UTC: rollback logic failed to propagate when canary nodes moved to 20% (missing tag in deploy job)
- Result: 20% of nodes had window_ms=10 after subsequent autoscale events.

Why small window_ms harms throughput (short note):
- Smaller windows => more frequent batch attempts with fewer requests/tokens per batch. Overhead per batch (serialization, kernel launch, KV prefill checks) becomes fixed cost that can't be amortized. Also prefill touchpoint frequency increases, stressing the prefill cache and causing evictions. If several nodes have this misconfig, global capacity for efficient batching decreases leading to upstream retries and client-side backpressure, further fragmenting token counts.

Mitigations tried during incident and immediate results:
- Emergency: Reverted canary change (set window_ms back to 50) on affected nodes via rwictl patch — immediate improvement in batch sizes and occupancy; throughput recovered to ~95% baseline within 8 minutes.
- Short-term: Increased prefill cache TTL by 30s across cluster — small win for repeated prefixes.
- Kinetic: Temporarily raised allocator small-slab pool by 25% on storefront nodes — reduced slab allocation errors but not long-term fix.

Follow-ups / things to validate (actionable list):
- Add a gating test in CI that runs a micro-batcher simulation: vary window_ms between 5-100ms and assert throughput degradation < 10% for synthetic mix.
- Add deploy-time check to ensure continuous_batch.window_ms changes are only allowed on full rollout with manual opt-in; block canary-only flips to <20ms automatically.
- Improve telemetry: emit per-node batch_quality metric = tokens_per_batch / attempts_per_sec and alert when below threshold for 5m.
- Revisit prefill eviction logic: add hysteresis so candidates near the threshold are not evicted more than once per X seconds.
- Root cause doc: follow up with a short postmortem and include the deploy job logs that missed the rollback tag.

Notes to self (loose):
- This incident felt like multiple interacting safe-to-ignore changes that combined into an emergent regression. Keep an eye out for coupling between batching config and allocator size.
- When triaging next time, first check per-node window_ms and batch_quality metric before assuming client-side change.
- Talk to release-eng about embedding an invariant test in CI for batching-related flags.

Open questions I couldn't answer in the window:
- Exactly which autoscale events caused the canary nodes to be stretched from 10% -> ~20%? Need to correlate autoscaler logs with deploy rollouts.
- Did any third-party onboarding client increase short-seq traffic coincidentally? Check APIGW logs for client id spikes.

Scratch commands useful for next on-call runbook (copy into runbook later):
- rwictl pods --label continuous-batcher -n inference
- rwictl exec -p {pod} -- cat /etc/continuous-batcher/config.yml
- kubectl logs -n inference {pod} -c batcher --since=15m | grep "built batch"
- elasticsearch query template: "service:batcher AND prefill_churn.rate:>3 AND window_ms:10 AND @timestamp:[now-30m TO now]"

End of notes.

(If anyone reading: this doc is a raw working draft. Will convert into a concise postmortem once we validate the autoscaler interaction.)
